seoTitle: How to Connect Zoom to Your GoHighLevel Calendar
metaDescription: Connect Zoom to your GoHighLevel calendar step by step, from the Connections settings page to authorizing Zoom, so meeting links generate automatically.
intro: Manually creating a Zoom link and pasting it into every booking confirmation doesn't scale past a handful of appointments a week. GoHighLevel has a native video conferencing connection built into its calendar settings that generates a fresh Zoom link automatically every time someone books, no copy-pasting required. This guide shows exactly where that setting lives, what the Zoom authorization screen looks like when you connect it, and what to check afterward so clients actually receive working meeting links.

steps.heading: Open Calendars, then Connections in Settings
steps.body: From the main GoHighLevel sidebar, go to Settings and choose Calendars. At the top of that page you'll find four tabs — Calendars, Meetings, Rentals, and Connections — and Connections is where every third-party tool your calendar can talk to lives, including video conferencing providers, not just calendar sync. On a fresh sub-account this page opens to an empty state under the Calendars tab reading "No connections found," with an Add new button, which is easy to mistake for the whole page rather than just one of its three sections.

image.caption: The Connections page under Settings, Calendars. Video conferencing tools like Zoom live in their own tab here, separate from calendar sync.

steps.heading: Switch to the Video conferencing tab and click Connect on Zoom
steps.body: Within Connections, click over to the Video conferencing tab. This section lists Google Meet, Zoom, and Microsoft Teams side by side, each with its own Connect button, and a short line explaining that connecting one lets GoHighLevel automatically generate a unique meeting link every time an appointment is scheduled. Google Meet has a dependency worth noting — GoHighLevel flags that it requires Google Calendar to be connected first — but Zoom has no such prerequisite, so you can connect it on its own.

image.caption: The Video conferencing section, listing Google Meet, Zoom, and Microsoft Teams with individual Connect buttons for each provider.

steps.heading: Sign in to Zoom and authorize the connection
steps.body: Clicking Connect opens Zoom's own sign-in screen in an overlay, complete with Zoom's branding and the usual email and password fields, plus SSO, Apple, Google, Facebook, and Microsoft as alternate sign-in options. Enter the credentials for the Zoom account you want GoHighLevel to book meetings through — this matters if your business has more than one Zoom account, since whichever one you authorize here is the one every future booking will use. After signing in, Zoom will ask you to approve the permissions GoHighLevel is requesting; accept, and control returns to the Connections page with Zoom now showing as connected.

image.caption: Zoom's sign-in screen appears in an overlay after clicking Connect, prompting you to log in with the Zoom account GoHighLevel should use.

steps.heading: Attach Zoom to the specific calendar or event type
steps.body: Connecting Zoom at the account level makes it available, but each individual calendar or appointment type still needs Zoom selected as its meeting location. Open the calendar you want to use it on, find the meeting location or conferencing setting, and choose Zoom from the list instead of a physical address or phone call. Skip this and clients booking that calendar won't get a Zoom link even though the integration itself is live — a common gap between "connected" and "actually being used."

steps.heading: Confirm the automatic link generation works
steps.body: Book a test appointment through the calendar's public booking page as if you were a client. If the connection is working, the confirmation screen and the confirmation email should both include a unique Zoom join link and dial-in details generated specifically for that booking, not a static link you set once. Check that the link actually opens a valid Zoom meeting a few minutes before the scheduled time, since a broken or expired authorization will still show a link in the email — it just won't connect to anything real.

steps.heading: Layer in reminders so clients actually show up
steps.body: With the link generating correctly, use GoHighLevel's workflow or appointment reminder tools to send that Zoom link again closer to meeting time — a confirmation email sent days in advance is easy to lose in an inbox. A reminder an hour or a day before, with the same Zoom details restated, meaningfully cuts down on no-shows for consultations, demos, and any other meeting type booked straight from your calendar.

faq.question: Do I need a paid Zoom account to connect it to GoHighLevel?
faq.answer: A standard Zoom account is generally sufficient to authorize the connection, though meeting length limits and participant caps still follow whatever Zoom plan that account is on.

faq.question: Will clients automatically receive the Zoom link after booking?
faq.answer: Yes — once Zoom is connected and set as the meeting location on a calendar, GoHighLevel generates a unique link for each booking and includes it in the confirmation email automatically.

faq.question: Can I disconnect Zoom from GoHighLevel later?
faq.answer: Yes, return to Settings, Calendars, Connections, Video conferencing, and you can disconnect or reconnect Zoom from the same panel at any time.

faq.question: Why isn't my calendar generating Zoom links even though Zoom shows as connected?
faq.answer: The account-level connection and a calendar's meeting location setting are separate. Open the specific calendar and confirm Zoom is selected as its conferencing option, not just connected at the account level.

faq.question: Does this integration work for recurring meetings?
faq.answer: Yes, it works on both one-time bookings and recurring appointment types, generating a fresh link for each occurrence in the same way.
